newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Parade of sail in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Parade of sail in Hong Kong.

text.p: Tall sailing ships paraded in stately procession past Hong Kong's harbour-side skyscrapers on Friday before the start of a race to Osaka to mark the Japanese city's centennial celebration as a modern port.

"The symbolism of the tall ships coming to Hong Kong, which is ending its 150-year history after the colonisation which started with the Opium War, is very significant," said race director Kaoru Ogimi, referring to the British colony's return to Chinese rule on July 1.
The ships from 18 countries and territories were in Hong Kong for a very different purpose than in the mid-1800s when the British sailed to China with opium, Ogimi said.

"Here, the ships are deliberately and specifically being used to carry the opposite message of 'Now we join hands across the sea to live and prosper in peace and harmony and mutual respect and understanding'," he told Reuters.
The ships will take a month for the 2,640 nautical mile race to Osaka, with several stops en route. Prizes will go to the winners but Ogimi said he preferred to call the event a "festival of sail".

The event has already been hit by tragedy. The Queen Charlotte, a New Zealand ship sailing to join the second leg off Japan, broke up in a tropical cyclone last week. The search for the five crew members was abandoned.
The ships range from Denmark's all-wood Jens Krogh built in 1899 to Russia's huge three-masted Pallada and its sister ship, the Dar Molodziezy from Poland.

About 30 tall ships and yachts paraded through Hong Kong harbour on Friday, and the number of ships was expected to swell to more than 50 by the time the fleet reached Osaka around April 27, organisers said.
